title: fix(plugin-audit): redaction runs open each checkpoint once; the sealer re-reads before a late checkpoint and drops a lost sequence's seed
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

Part of #31908 (slice P4a)
Fixes #32737

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读 (Maintainer quick read)

- 改了什么：审计脱敏迁移在一次运行里对每个检查点只验签、重建根、开种子各一次（原来是每行一次）；封存器写 late 检查点前重读该窗口已列出的行并剔除；插入因序号已被别的检查点占用而失败时，删掉自己刚封的种子。规格包只改一句过时注释。
- 为什么改：每行一次的成本随窗口行数平方增长，用 KMS 时每行一次远程调用；两个封存器租约重叠时，late 检查点可能把同一行封两次；序号丢失时会留下孤儿种子。
- 风险与回滚：判定规则与拒绝理由不变，现有脱敏与封存 pin 全部原样通过。唯一可见差别：一次运行里打开某检查点时遇到的故障只遇一次，该检查点列出的每一行都按同一理由拒绝，重跑会再试。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`amendment-writer.ts` 的 `admitted` / `opened` / `open`；`sealer.ts` 的 `writeCheckpoint`（late 分支与插入失败分支）；`audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts` 新增的计数 describe。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal/audit-seal-sealer.test.ts src/audit-seal/audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts`，预期 2 个文件、46 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。本切片第 5 项（迁移命令持 `audit.sealer` 锁）未做，待席位决策，见 Acceptance notes。

## What changes

1. **The redaction amendment writer admits and opens each checkpoint once per run (#32737).** `amendment-writer.ts`: the listing now holds one `ListedCheckpoint` per stored checkpoint, shared by every row that checkpoint lists. `admitted()` verifies its signature once per run through the same `admits()` rule (D6, the one the verifier shares). `opened()` rebuilds its root from `leaf_hashes`, reads its seed's `sys_secret` row and opens the seed through the crypto provider once per run, and keeps a row id to leaf hash map, so the per-row `row_ids.indexOf` scan is gone too. Each answer is kept once it settles, refusals and faults included. A checkpoint that does not verify still refuses every row it lists, and a seed that is missing or does not open still refuses every row it sealed, with the same reason text as before.
2. **N1: a `late` checkpoint re-reads its window's lists.** `sealer.ts` `writeCheckpoint`: once the chain's head is known, and before anything is encrypted or signed, the window's stored checkpoints (every chain's) are re-read (`listedIn`) and each row one of them already lists is dropped. A chain left with no row writes nothing and seals no seed. A checkpoint stored after the head was known takes a sequence at or past this one, so the unique `(sealed_object, chain_key, sequence)` index refuses whichever insert lands second; the code comment states that invariant.
3. **N2: a lost sequence's seed is dropped.** `sealer.ts`, the insert's catch: when the read-back finds a checkpoint at this sequence holding another `seed_handle`, the unique index proves this seed can never be stored, so `dropAuditSealSecret` removes it before the throw. When nothing is read back, whether the insert stored is unknown, and the seed is kept as before (M1).
4. **N3: the keyset tie arm is pinned.** Rows of one `created_at` straddle the 500-row page boundary, and each row is read exactly once. The keyset was already right, so there is no code change; the ablation below shows the pin bites.
5. **Spec comment.** `platform-object-names.ts`: the `plugin-audit` group's comment said `sys_audit_amendment` is "the one name in this group the package does not register". `AuditPlugin` registers it in its manifest objects and provisions it (`audit-plugin.ts` lines 344 and 872), so the comment now says the package registers every name in the group. Comment only; the comment text ships inside spec's built `dist` chunks, so the changeset lists `@objectstack/spec` as a patch (the version group is fixed, so this adds no extra bump).

**Not in this PR: slice item 5, the `os migrate audit-*` commands holding `audit.sealer` for their run.** Withheld for a decision; see Acceptance notes.

## Tests

Tests first: `d41ddf570` adds the pins, `88a4abc22` adds the fixes.

- `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`
  - N1: a second sealer runs right after this pass's one read of the horizon's checkpoints and seals the late row. This pass writes nothing (`runPass()` answers 0), exactly one checkpoint lists the row, and every `ledger_probe` seed row is named by a checkpoint.
  - N2: a second sealer stores sequence 0 between this pass's S1 re-read and its insert. The insert fails on the unique index, and the only `ledger_probe` seed row left is the stored checkpoint's.
  - N3: 495 rows a second apart, then 15 rows of one instant. Every row is sealed, in order, and each is returned by exactly one page.
- `audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts`, new top-level describe on its own live boot (SQLite, the plugin's own sealer). Three chains of four mail-body copies are sealed in one window. org_b's checkpoint signature is replaced, so it does not verify, and org_c's seed ciphertext is replaced, so it does not open. Then one `migrateMailLogBodyCopies` apply run is made under counting spies that call through.
  - Each checkpoint is verified once: `{ org_a: 1, org_b: 1, org_c: 1 }`.
  - Each seed reached is opened once: org_a and org_c once each, and org_b's never, because its checkpoint does not verify.
  - The report is 12 scanned, 4 rewritten, 8 refused and 0 failures. The live check reads every org_a row `redacted`.
  - Every org_b row is refused with "checkpoint 0 that lists it does not verify under a trusted signing key". Every org_c row is refused with "the seed of checkpoint 0 that sealed it does not open". All eight keep their body.

Every existing pin in both files is unchanged and green.

## Acceptance notes

- **Slice item 5 (the migrate commands hold `audit.sealer`) is not done, and needs a ruling.** The dispatch's mechanism assumption was that reusing the sealer's own acquisition in the commands keeps a live sealer in another process from interleaving. Measured statically on `19cc8976b`, it does not:
  - The sealer's `acquireLock` (`sealer.ts` 254-271) takes `cluster.lock` when a `cluster` service is registered, and otherwise a module-level in-process lock.
  - All three commands boot through `bootSchemaStack`, which builds `new Runtime({ cluster: false })` (`packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts` 1374-1375). `Runtime` registers `ClusterServicePlugin` only when `config.cluster !== false` (`packages/runtime/src/runtime.ts` 88), so the one-shot boot has no `cluster` service, and reuse lands on the in-process lock.
  - Only `os serve` composes a cross-process lock driver, from `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` / `OS_REDIS_URL` (`serve.ts` 3204-3427). The default `memory` driver is per-process by design (`service-cluster` index.ts 16).
  - So a lock taken this way excludes no sealer on any deployment. Shipping it would advertise exclusion the runtime does not deliver.
  - The route that delivers it means composing the cluster driver into the one-shot boot (`schema-migrate.ts`, outside this slice's file surface). That is a new mechanism, which the dispatch ruled out.
  - The options and their costs are in the os-dev report on #31908.
- **A fault met while opening a checkpoint is met once per run.** If reading the seed's row or opening the seed throws, every row that checkpoint lists is refused this run with the same reason, where before each row tried again. That is the "reuse the result for every row" of #32737. A re-run opens it afresh.
- **"Once per run" is once per writer run.** The hot run and the archive run of one command each build their own `RedactionAmender`, so a checkpoint whose rows sit in both stores is opened once in each. Sharing one writer across both runs would touch the runner files, which are outside this slice.
- **Timing.** The branch is 13 commits behind `origin/main`. None of them touch `plugin-audit`, the spec constants file or the CLI migrate commands, and a local `merge-tree` is clean.
